PR #1674 pairs the two absences without connecting them either, naming "presentation-registry anchoring or observer-based TEL retrieval" as the follow-up work. 2026-10-03: half answered. The Grantee checks it, against a TEL it must already hold locally; retrieval has not arrived, and the tests preload the foreign TEL to "Simulate the future observer retrieval layer" ([section 7.3](#10-still-absent)). The Observer connection is still unbuilt, and still no written source connects the two.

#### Question 8: Two incompatible bespoke origin ACDCs share a name {#10-q-two-bespoke-origins}

New: two incompatible bespoke origin ACDCs share a name. #1613 requires the self-issued bespoke origin to use a blinded state registry for its Issuer authentication, or the correlation resistance a presentation registry buys is handed back at the origin node ([section 3](#10-two-jobs)). #1627's SEDI "recipe" pattern specifies the opposite — no registry, no anchor, bare attached signatures, because it is one-time use. Both are Sam, three weeks apart, and both are coherent for their own purpose; they are two different bespoke ACDCs for two different jobs. But neither document says the other exists, and the shared name invites the wrong one. Any worked example that combines a presentation registry with a #1627-style recipe origin is wrong in a way neither source warns about — it yields a correlatable presentation and a `grant` whose perpetual verifiability the origin ACDC cannot carry. 2026-10-03: unchanged. keripy constructs neither kind of bespoke origin together with a presentation registry ([section 3](#10-two-jobs)).

#### Question 9: keripy refuses `grant`s for reasons no specification states {#10-q-unspecified-refusals}

New 2026-10-03 (`raw/16` section 8 item 13). Four [code] refusal grounds — an unbound declared registry, an `a.rd` with no top-level `rd`, a compact `a` on a registry-backed ACDC, an undisclosed `A` entry on one — have no [spec] or [spec-next] counterpart ([section 8](#10-adversarial)). The open question is which side moves: the specifications adopting the rules, or keripy relaxing the ones a peer cannot be expected to know.

#### Question 10: The code's requirement is unconditional, and #1613's is not {#10-q-unconditional}

New 2026-10-03 (`raw/16` section 8 item 11). #1613 applies the anchoring requirement "when the Issuee is the Grantor of that IPEX" (#1613 > Registry Anchored Granted ACDCs). keripy applies it to every declaration in the granted DAG, whoever sends ([section 7](#10-keripy-verifier)). The two agree when a holder presents its own credential. They differ for #1613's Anchoring Requirement Complication section, where "an ACDC is presented as evidence, but the Issuee AID is unrelated to the Discloser's AID". Under keripy's rule nobody can present such an ACDC unless its Issuee writes this `grant`'s SAID into its registry. That may be intended — it is the strongest reading of "an imposter … can't avoid the requirement" — but it makes a presentation-registry ACDC unusable as third-party evidence, and neither #1613 nor the code says whether that was weighed. A scoping question, not a bug report.

#### Question 11: Single versus double authentication for a non-sender Issuee {#10-q-single-vs-double}

New 2026-10-03 (`raw/16` section 8 item 12). #1613 says every Grantor must endorse and that a registry-anchored `grant` is "always double-authenticated"; keripy since `b7c170f93` accepts a proxy-sent `grant` whose Issuee participates only through the registry binding ([section 6](#10-registrar-and-kram)). Deliberate, and defensible on its face, but the design document and the code now disagree about what a Grantor is, and the endorser index does not list registry-only Issuees, so business logic that finds a holder's presentations through `eidx` will miss them. Open: whether #1613's text should move to match the code, or the reverse.

#### Question 12: Fail-closed discovery may rule out selective aggregate disclosure {#10-q-aggregate-disclosure}

New 2026-10-03, unverified: fail-closed discovery may rule out selective aggregate disclosure of a registry-backed ACDC (`raw/16` section 8 item 14). For `a` the cost is small, since tests compact nested blocks and keep the top level expanded. For `A`, rejecting any undisclosed aggregate entry appears to rule out selective disclosure altogether. The SEDI Age credential has both a top-level `rd` and an `A`, and no IPEX test at `80f77b73b` presents it. `raw/16` did not check how keripy represents an undisclosed aggregate element. If it is not a mapping, an Age credential cannot be selectively presented through keripy IPEX at this pin, which would collide with the age-proof design in `raw/11` and #1098.
